segments.md:
# Calendar

Four views — day, week, month, and year — are one surface seen through a moving,
zooming **focus rectangle** over a month's day-grid. The whole grid is the month;
a spring shrinks the rectangle onto one row for the week, one cell for the day.
Each cell is just its grid slot mapped through that rectangle, so changing view is
one continuous zoom. As a cell grows its events reshape from stacked chips into
placed time-blocks; drag one to reschedule. Year is the same surface a step
further out, each month folding into a mini.

── the two palettes — every color in the app, named by role ──

Light is house San Francisco: `background`, `line`, `text`, `textMuted`,
`textFaint`, `accent`, `control` and `controlSelected` are the preset's own
values, to the byte.

Dark deliberately is not, and the reason is the grid. House dark is
stepped — background → surface → control each a visible rung apart (ΔE 5.4 and
7.7). A month is a 2D tiling of 42 equal cells, and stepped surfaces there
read as corduroy, so this palette is flat and deep instead (the same two
gaps, ΔE 2.6 and 2.5) with one bright exception: `controlSelected` sits 4 L*
above house so the selection still pops out of the quiet field.
`textMuted` drops ~8 L* to hold its hierarchy against the flatter
surfaces. `text` and `accent` are house exactly, in both modes.

This is the corpus's only 2D-tiled surface — the tracker is a list, with
rules between its rows, and runs house dark untouched. So these stay the
app's own records rather than a second preset: one example is not a pattern.

segments.html:
theme CalendarLight [

    weekendBg = #F1F4F8, todayBg = #DCE9FF, dropTargetBg = #C7DDFF, dropTargetRing = #2E6FE0,
    line = #DBE1E9, gridLine = #E4E9EF, text = #1B2733, textMuted = #6C7A88,
    textFaint = #AAB4BE, dayNumber = #2A3542, bodyText = #3E4C59, hourLabel = #99A5B0,
    accent = #2E6FE0, accentSecondary = #12A594, currentDayText = #2E6FE0, todayText = #2E6FE0,
    control = #E7EBF1, controlSelected = #D3E2FC, fieldBg = #FFFFFF, fieldEdge = #DBE1E9,
    sectionBg = #F1F5F9, sectionOpenBg = #E6EEF8, miniBg = #FFFFFF, miniCurrentBg = #E7F0FF,
    miniDayText = #3E4C59, miniDayFaint = #BFC8D2, holidayBg = #DCF3E4, holidayText = #1E7A44,
    astroBg = #EBE6FB, astroText = #5B3FB8, milestoneBg = #FBEFD6, milestoneText = #9A6A11,

segments.md:
## Event

Morphs between a stacked month-chip and a placed time-block as its day zooms
(`rowBlock`), and shrinks to a single dot in the year view (`app.yearZoom`).

segments.html:
class Ev [ clip = true,

    rowBlock: number = { (parent as Cell).rowBlock },
    timeLabel: string = { app.shortTime(:start) },

    cornerRadius = { app.lerp(5, 1.5, app.yearZoom) },
    fill = { app.mix(app.catFill(:category), provided("theme").accent, app.yearZoom) },
    opacity = { app.dragId == :id && app.dragging ? 0.2 : 1 },
    x = { app.lerp(4, (parent.width - 3) / 2, app.yearZoom) },
    width = { app.lerp(parent.width - 8, 3, app.yearZoom) },
    y      = { app.lerp(app.lerp(26 + rowIndex * 20, :start / 1440 * parent.height, classroot.rowBlock),
                        parent.height - 6, app.yearZoom) },
    height = { app.lerp(app.lerp(17, Math.max(18, (:end - :start) / 1440 * parent.height), classroot.rowBlock),
                        3, app.yearZoom) },

    rail: View [ width = 3, height = 100%, fill = { app.catText(:category) }, opacity = { classroot.rowBlock } ],
    text: View [ x = 8, y = 2, opacity = { 1 - app.yearZoom },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 6 ],
        tm: Text [ fontSize = 10, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false, textColor = { app.catText(:category) }, text = { classroot.timeLabel } ],
        ti: Text [ fontSize = 10, fontWeight = regular, wrap = false, textColor = { app.catText(:category) }, text = { :title } ]
        ],

    onPointerDown(e: PointerEvent) { app.startDrag(:id, :title, :category, timeLabel, this.width, this.height, e.x, e.y) },
    onPointerMove()  { app.dragMove() },
    onPointerUp(e: PointerUpEvent)   { app.dropDrag(e.rootX, e.rootY, e.canceled) },

    // The hold moves this chip's touch claim to the press-and-hold (a drag view
    // that also holds claims nothing at touchdown) — a quick swipe over a chip
    // pans the page; press-and-hold picks the event up, and the hold itself
    // lifts the ghost so the pickup is visible before the finger moves.

    onHold()       { app.armDrag() },
    onClick()      { app.selectEvent(:id, :y + "-" + :m + "-" + :d) }
    ]

segments.md:
## Cell

One day of the surface — its rectangle is its month-grid slot mapped through the
focus rectangle, so the same object is a month cell, a week column, or a full day.
In the year view (`app.yearZoom`) it re-lays-out into the current month's mini rather than
scaling, keeping its text crisp.

segments.html:
class Cell [ clip = true,

    rowBlock: number = { :row == app.anchorRow ? app.blockness : 0 },

    x = { app.lerp(app.pad + app.gutter + (:col - app.c0) * app.colW + app.gap / 2, app.slotX + 10 + :col * app.miniCellW, app.yearZoom) },
    y = { app.lerp(app.headH + (:row - app.r0) * app.rowH + app.gap / 2, app.slotY + 34 + :row * app.miniRowH, app.yearZoom) },
    width = { app.lerp(app.colW - app.gap, app.miniCellW, app.yearZoom) },
    height = { app.lerp(app.rowH - app.gap, app.miniRowH, app.yearZoom) },

    // the fill fades as the cell becomes a column, then melts to the mini's
    // highlight in the year view; only the drop target draws a ring

    bg: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, cornerRadius = 8,
        opacity = { 1 - 0.82 * classroot.rowBlock },
        fill = { app.mix(
              :key == app.dropKey ? provided("theme").dropTargetBg
            : :today              ? app.mix(provided("theme").todayBg, provided("theme").cellBg, classroot.rowBlock)
            : !:inMonth           ? provided("theme").outOfMonthBg
            : :weekend            ? provided("theme").weekendBg
            :                       provided("theme").cellBg,
            provided("theme").miniCurrentBg, app.yearZoom) },
        stroke = { :key == app.dropKey ? stroke(2, app.mix(provided("theme").dropTargetRing, provided("theme").miniCurrentBg, app.yearZoom)) : null } ],

    // current-day accent bar, fading in as the cell fills the surface

    mark: View [ width = 100%, height = 3, fill = { provided("theme").accent }, visible = { :current }, opacity = { classroot.rowBlock } ],
    num: Text [ x = { app.lerp(11, parent.width / 2 - 5, app.yearZoom) }, y = { app.lerp(7, 2, app.yearZoom) },
        fontSize = { app.lerp(13, 9, app.yearZoom) }, wrap = false, fontWeight = semibold,
        opacity = { :inMonth ? 1 : 1 - app.yearZoom },
        textColor = { :current ? provided("theme").currentDayText : :today ? provided("theme").todayText : :inMonth ? provided("theme").dayNumber : provided("theme").textFaint },
        text = { "" + :num } ],
    dow: Text [ x = 34, y = 8, fontSize = 11, wrap = false, opacity = { classroot.rowBlock },
        textColor = { :current ? provided("theme").currentDayText : provided("theme").textMuted }, text = { :dow } ],
    Ev [ datapath = :events[], key = :id ],

    onClick() { app.pickDay(:key) }
    ]

segments.md:
## Year minis

The year view's twelve small months. The current month is drawn by the main
`board` folding into its slot, so only the other eleven come from here.

segments.html:
class MiniDay [ width = { app.miniCellW }, height = { app.miniRowH },
    x = { :col * app.miniCellW }, y = { :row * app.miniRowH },
    n: Text [ width = 100%, textAlign = center, y = 1, fontSize = 9, wrap = false,
        textColor = { :today ? provided("theme").accent : :inMonth ? provided("theme").miniDayText : provided("theme").miniDayFaint },
        text = { :inMonth ? "" + :num : "" } ],
    dot: View [ x = center, y = { parent.height - 4 }, width = 3, height = 3,
        cornerRadius = 2, fill = { provided("theme").accent }, visible = { :has } ]
    ]


class MiniMonth [ cornerRadius = 12, clip = true, fill = { provided("theme").miniBg },
    width = { app.miniW }, height = { app.miniH },
    x = { app.pad + :mcol * (app.miniW + app.gap) }, y = { app.pad + :mrow * (app.miniH + app.gap) },
    visible = { :m != app.month },      // the current month is the folding board, not a mini

    name: Text [ x = 14, y = 11, fontSize = 13, fontWeight = semibold,
        textColor = { :m == app.month ? provided("theme").todayText : provided("theme").dayNumber }, text = { :name } ],
    grid: View [ x = 10, y = 34, width = { parent.width - 20 }, height = { parent.height - 44 },
        MiniDay [ datapath = :cells[] ]
        ],

    onClick() { app.pickMonth(:m) }
    ]

segments.md:
## Paging arrow

`dir` says everything: −1 turns the chevron left and pages back, +1 right and
forward — the same disclosure mark, at the same weight, as every other chevron
in the app.

segments.html:
class NavArrow extends Control [ width = 36, height = 34, cornerRadius = 10,
    dir: number = 1,
    fill = { pressed ? provided("theme").controlSelected : provided("theme").control },
    g: ChevronIcon [ iconSize = 15, x = center, y = center,
        dir = { classroot.dir < 0 ? "left" : "right" },
        ink = { classroot.pressed || classroot.hovered ? provided("theme").text : provided("theme").textMuted } ],
    press() { app.step(dir) }
    ]

segments.md:
## Detail section

A collapsible field in the event panel — a spring-driven height, one open at a
time. Its input two-way binds to the event property named by `field`, so an edit
writes straight to the record.

segments.html:
class DetailSection [ clip = true, cornerRadius = 10, fill = { provided("theme").sectionBg },
    idx: number = 0,
    label: string = "",
    field: string = "",
    isOpen: boolean = { app.openSection == idx },
    width = 100%, height = 46,
    Spring [ attribute = height, to = { isOpen ? 156 : 46 }, stiffness = 210, damping = 24 ],

    hdr: Control [ width = 100%, height = 46, padding = [0, 11, 0, 15],
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x ],      // each child centers itself, as icons do
        lbl: Text [ y = center, fontSize = 12, fontWeight = bold, wrap = false, letterSpacing = 1,
            textColor = { classroot.isOpen ? provided("theme").text : provided("theme").textMuted }, text = { classroot.label } ],
        Spacer [ ],

        // open/closed as minus/plus, drawn, in the same muted ink as the label

        MinusIcon [ iconSize = 15, visible = { classroot.isOpen }, ink = { provided("theme").textMuted } ],
        PlusIcon [ iconSize = 15, visible = { !classroot.isOpen }, ink = { provided("theme").textMuted } ],
        press() { app.openSection = classroot.idx }
        ],

    // A TextInput derives its own chrome from the house role names (`surface`,
    // `line`); those derives yield to an author assignment, so the field is
    // styled here in the app's own vocabulary, focus edge included.

    content: TextInput [ x = 13, y = 50, width = { parent.width - 26 }, height = { parent.height - 60 }, multiline = true, wrap = true,
        fontSize = 16, textColor = { provided("theme").bodyText }, placeholder = { "Add " + classroot.field },
        fill = { provided("theme").fieldBg },
        stroke = { stroke(1, this.focused ? provided("theme").accent : provided("theme").fieldEdge) },
        text <-> { classroot.field } ],
    open: State [ applied = { isOpen }, fill = { provided("theme").sectionOpenBg } ]
    ]


// This app is a fixed window — every view and interaction lives in-frame, and
// the browser must never scroll the app itself. The App's clip **contains**:
// the detail panel parked beyond the right edge (x > width, sliding in via
// panelInset) paints nowhere, adds no document scroll extent, and cannot be
// focus-scrolled into view.

// Below the floor the calendar degrades instead of adapting (the grid needs its
// rows), so it declares one and the stage pans. The floor is phone-honest:
// with the bar tiering to two rows and the detail panel overlaying instead of
// insetting (below), nothing but the grid itself decides the minimum — seven
// legible columns, the same budget a phone-native month view spends.

App [ minWidth = 360, minHeight = 420, appName = "Declare Calendar",
    fill = { provided("theme").background }, fontFamily = ["system-ui", "sans-serif"],

segments.md:
Colors are two role-named palettes; `theme` swaps between them. `themeMode`
is Light / Dark / Auto — Auto follows the environment: what the host provides as `dark` when this
app runs embedded (a desktop passing its appearance through), else the OS
through `app.dark`.

The record is the house preset extended, not replaced: the standard
tokens underneath, this app's own values over them, and its domain names
(weekendBg, holidayText, miniCurrentBg …) alongside. A standard control
dropped in here finds every token it consults, while the calendar keeps
its own palette — the spread only adds the tokens the app never named.

segments.html:
theme = { { ...(app.isDark ? SanFranciscoDark : SanFrancisco), ...(app.isDark ? CalendarDark : CalendarLight) } },
    themeMode: string = "auto",

    // Auto's environment: what a host provides first (a desktop or page that
    // embeds the calendar decides dark for it), else the system preference.

    isDark: boolean = { app.themeMode == "auto"
        ? hostProvided("dark", app.dark)
        : app.themeMode == "dark" },

    // layout constants

    barH: number = { app.barNarrow ? 100 : 60 },     // two rows when narrow; everything below derives
    pad: number = 20,
    gap: number = 8,

segments.md:
Responsive chrome, all from the window width. As it narrows the
Light/Auto/Dark switch drops out, then the tabs shrink to single letters
(D/W/M/Y). Thresholds are sized to the widest view so the bar never flickers
when you switch views at a fixed width.

segments.html:
showTheme: boolean = { app.width >= 1030 },
    tabsCompact: boolean = { app.width < 910 },
    brandCompact: boolean = { app.width < 640 },     // "Declare Calendar" → "Declare" (still the way home)
    barNarrow: boolean = { app.width < 560 },        // the bar tiers to two rows: controls above, date nav below
    tabW: number = { app.tabsCompact ? 44 : 74 },
    tabsW: number = { 4 * app.tabW },

    // The date block is a fixed width per mode, from the widest label that mode
    // can ever show — measured, in the face the title actually renders in, so
    // a font or locale change moves it with no constant to retune. It must not
    // follow the current label: the arrows sit at its edges, so a width that
    // tracked "May 4" and then "September 30" would shift them as you page.

    titleFace: object = { providedTextStyle(({ fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "semibold" })) },
    widestOf(samples: string[]) -> number {
        return Math.max(0, ...samples.map((t) => measureText(t, app.titleFace).width))
        },
    dateW: number = { Math.ceil(app.widestOf(
        app.mode == "week"  ? ["September 30 – October 31"]           // the cross-month week, longest names
      : app.mode == "day"   ? ["Wednesday, September 30"]              // longest weekday + longest month
      : app.mode == "month" ? ["September 2088"]
      :                       ["2088"]) + 14) },
    panelOverlay: boolean = { app.width < 720 },     // the detail panel overlays the grid instead of insetting it
    panelW: number = { Math.min(340, app.width - 32) },

    // view + paging state

    mode: string = "month",

    // Where the user has paged to — the only date cells, and all navigation
    // writes. `0` / `""` mean "today"; a bare-literal default owns a cell, so
    // writing one wakes every reader.

    navYear: number = 0,
    navMonth: number = 0,      // month is 1-based
    navKey: string = "",

    // The visible date, derived. A sentinel rather than a literal date keeps the
    // declaration true at construction, where the focus rectangle's springs
    // take their snap.

    // Today is the clock's, so it turns over at midnight.

    clock: Time [ tick = day ],
    year: number = { app.navYear == 0 ? app.clock.year : app.navYear },
    month: number = { app.navMonth == 0 ? app.clock.month : app.navMonth },
    todayKey: string = { app.clock.year + "-" + app.clock.month + "-" + app.clock.day },
    anchorKey: string = { app.navKey == "" ? app.todayKey : app.navKey },
    monthRows: number = { app.computeMonthRows() },
    yearSeen: boolean = false,
    selectedId: number = -1,
    openSection: number = 0,

segments.md:
The address is environment-aware: standalone, the fixture sits beside the
app; hosted (the desktop passes env.base — its own transport's path to
this app's home), the same relative address resolves through that base.
`auto` loads it either way: the url is the reactive thing, and when a
late-landing base changes it the source fetches the right address.

Edits write straight into this source (`app.data.set`). It loads once
and nothing fetches it again, so there is no refresh to overwrite them
and no need for a working copy; a source that refetches would want one,
as the tracker's `db` is.

segments.html: data: DataSource [ auto = true, url = { hostProvided("base", "") + "data/events.json" } ],

segments.md:
The model is derived, not built: `cal.contents` recomputes when the visible
month or the events change, and keyed replication (`:key`, `:id`) makes each
recompute cost only the days that changed. The year grid is its own
derivation, deferred until first visited and memoized on the year.

segments.html:
cal: Dataset [ contents = { app.buildModel() } ],
    yearCal: Dataset [ contents = { app.yearSeen ? app.buildMonths() : app.emptyYear() } ],

    // the detail panel slides in on this value; the body shrinks by the same amount

    panelInset: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = panelInset, to = { app.selectedId >= 0 ? app.panelW : 0 }, stiffness = 240, damping = 30 ],

    // geometry

    bodyW: number = { app.width - (app.panelOverlay ? 0 : app.panelInset) },   // an overlaying panel never squeezes the grid
    bodyH: number = { app.height - app.barH },
    headH: number = 30,
    miniW: number = { (app.bodyW - 2 * app.pad - app.gap * 3) / 4 },
    miniH: number = { (app.bodyH - 2 * app.pad - app.gap * 2) / 3 },
    miniCellW: number = { (app.miniW - 20) / 7 },
    miniRowH: number = { (app.miniH - 44) / 6 },

segments.md:
The focus rectangle: (c0,r0) is where the frame starts, (nc,nr) how many
columns/rows it spans. Month is the whole grid; week springs onto the anchor
row, day onto the anchor cell. Only a view switch moves the four springs.

segments.html:
anchorCol: number = { app.gridIndexOf(app.anchorKey) % 7 },
    anchorRow: number = { Math.floor(app.gridIndexOf(app.anchorKey) / 7) },
    c0To: number = { app.mode == "day" ? app.anchorCol : 0 },
    r0To: number = { app.mode == "week" || app.mode == "day" ? app.anchorRow : 0 },
    ncTo: number = { app.mode == "day" ? 1 : 7 },
    nrTo: number = { app.mode == "week" || app.mode == "day" ? 1 : app.monthRows },
    c0: number = 0,
    r0: number = 0,
    nc: number = 7,
    nr: number = 6,
    Spring [ attribute = c0, to = { app.c0To }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    Spring [ attribute = r0, to = { app.r0To }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    Spring [ attribute = nc, to = { app.ncTo }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    Spring [ attribute = nr, to = { app.nrTo }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],
    colW: number = { (app.bodyW - 2 * app.pad - app.gutter) / app.nc },
    rowH: number = { (app.bodyH - app.headH) / app.nr },

    // 0 = month chips, 1 = time blocks. Keyed on the focus span (one focused
    // row **is** a time view), never on pixel height: a short-landscape day
    // still resolves to blocks, and a tall monitor's month can never start
    // half-morphing its chips. Riding `nr` also keeps the morph continuous:
    // chips hold shape while the focus zooms, then resolve into blocks over
    // the last row of travel.

    blockness: number = { app.clamp(2 - app.nr, 0, 1) },

    gutter: number = { app.blockness * 52 },                             // hour-label gutter, opens in time views

segments.md:
Year zoom: `yearZoom` (0→1) shrinks the month surface into its slot in the 4×3 year
grid while the other eleven months resolve around it. `yearScale` scales the
surface and the surrounding grid in lock-step.

segments.html:
myCol: number = { (app.month - 1) % 4 },
    myRow: number = { Math.floor((app.month - 1) / 4) },
    slotX: number = { app.pad + app.myCol * (app.miniW + app.gap) },
    slotY: number = { app.pad + app.myRow * (app.miniH + app.gap) },
    yearScale: number = { app.lerp(app.bodyW / app.miniW, 1, app.yearZoom) },
    yearZoom: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = yearZoom, to = { app.mode == "year" ? 1 : 0 }, stiffness = 150, damping = 24, mass = 0.9, epsilon = 0.002 ],

    periodLabel: string = {
        app.mode == "year"  ? "" + app.year
      : app.mode == "month" ? app.monthName(app.month) + " " + app.year
      : app.mode == "week"  ? app.weekLabel(app.anchorKey)
      :                       app.dayLabel(app.anchorKey) },

    // ── helpers ──

    lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number) -> number { return a + (b - a) * t },
    clamp(v: number, a: number, b: number) -> number { return Math.max(a, Math.min(b, v)) },

    // blend two 0xRRGGBB colors channel-wise

    mix(a: number, b: number, t: number) -> number {
        const c = (x, y) => Math.round(x + (y - x) * t)
        return (c((a >> 16) & 255, (b >> 16) & 255) << 16) | (c((a >> 8) & 255, (b >> 8) & 255) << 8) | c(a & 255, b & 255)
        },
    monthName(m: number) -> string { return ["January","February","March","April","May","June","July","August","September","October","November","December"][m - 1] },
    dowName(i: number) -> string { return ["Sun","Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat"][i] },
    dowLong(i: number) -> string { return ["Sunday","Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday"][i] },
    keyOf(dt: object) -> string { return dt.getFullYear() + "-" + (dt.getMonth() + 1) + "-" + dt.getDate() },
    parseKey(k: string) -> object { const p = k.split("-").map(Number); return new Date(p[0], p[1] - 1, p[2]) },
    gridIndexOf(key: string) -> number {                       // a day's 0..41 slot in the month grid
        const first = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1)
        const start = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1 - first.getDay())
        const d = app.parseKey(key)
        return Math.round((Date.UTC(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate())
                         - Date.UTC(start.getFullYear(), start.getMonth(), start.getDate())) / 86400000)
        },
    shortTime(min: number) -> string {
        const h = Math.floor(min / 60), mm = min % 60, ap = h < 12 ? "a" : "p"
        let hh = h % 12; if (hh == 0) hh = 12
        return mm == 0 ? hh + ap : hh + ":" + (mm < 10 ? "0" + mm : "" + mm) + ap
        },
    hourLabel(h: number) -> string { const ap = h < 12 ? "AM" : "PM"; let hh = h % 12; if (hh == 0) hh = 12; return hh + " " + ap },
    weekLabel(k: string) -> string {
        const d = app.parseKey(k)
        const s = new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate() - d.getDay())
        const e = new Date(s.getFullYear(), s.getMonth(), s.getDate() + 6)
        return app.monthName(s.getMonth() + 1) + " " + s.getDate() + " – "
             + (s.getMonth() == e.getMonth() ? "" : app.monthName(e.getMonth() + 1) + " ") + e.getDate()
        },
    dayLabel(k: string) -> string { const d = app.parseKey(k); return app.dowLong(d.getDay()) + ", " + app.monthName(d.getMonth() + 1) + " " + d.getDate() },

    // -> number, not Color: these return a concrete 0xRRGGBB (theme tokens are
    // never null at read time), and number is what mix() blends — a nullable
    // Color return would refuse every mix(catFill(…), …) call site.

    catFill(c: string) -> number { const t = provided("theme"); return c == "holiday" ? t.holidayBg : c == "astro" ? t.astroBg : c == "milestone" ? t.milestoneBg : t.defaultBg },
    catText(c: string) -> number { const t = provided("theme"); return c == "holiday" ? t.holidayText : c == "astro" ? t.astroText : c == "milestone" ? t.milestoneText : t.defaultText },

    eventsOn(all: array, y: number, m: number, d: number) -> array {
        return all.filter(e => e.y == y && e.m == m && e.d == d).sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start || a.id - b.id)
        },
    computeMonthRows() {
        const first = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1)
        return Math.ceil((first.getDay() + new Date(this.year, this.month, 0).getDate()) / 7)
        },

segments.md:
## The model
`buildModel` builds the visible month's grid, each day holding its events —
the data's own records, so an event row reads and writes its record.
`buildMonths` builds the year's twelve minis; its only tracked input is the
year, so it rebuilds once a year and never on a view switch.

segments.html:
buildModel() {
        const all = app.data.read(["events"]) ?? []
        const cols = [0,1,2,3,4,5,6].map(i => ({ name: app.dowName(i), col: i }))
        const hours = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, h) => ({ h: h, label: app.hourLabel(h) }))
        const first = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1)
        const start = new Date(this.year, this.month - 1, 1 - first.getDay())
        const rows = app.computeMonthRows()
        const grid = []
        for (let i = 0; i < rows * 7; i++) {
            const dt = new Date(start.getFullYear(), start.getMonth(), start.getDate() + i)
            const row = Math.floor(i / 7)
            grid.push({ key: app.keyOf(dt), num: dt.getDate(), dow: app.dowName(dt.getDay()), col: i % 7, row: row,
                        inMonth: dt.getMonth() == this.month - 1, weekend: dt.getDay() == 0 || dt.getDay() == 6,
                        today: app.keyOf(dt) == this.todayKey, current: app.keyOf(dt) == this.anchorKey,
                        events: app.eventsOn(all, dt.getFullYear(), dt.getMonth() + 1, dt.getDate()) })
            }
        return { grid: grid, cols: cols, hours: hours }
        },
    buildMonths() {
        const all = app.data.value != null ? app.data.value.events : []
        const months = []
        for (let m = 1; m <= 12; m++) {
            const st = new Date(this.year, m - 1, 1 - new Date(this.year, m - 1, 1).getDay())
            const cells = []
            for (let i = 0; i < 42; i++) {
                const dt = new Date(st.getFullYear(), st.getMonth(), st.getDate() + i)
                cells.push({ num: dt.getDate(), col: i % 7, row: Math.floor(i / 7), inMonth: dt.getMonth() == m - 1,
                             today: app.keyOf(dt) == this.todayKey,
                             has: dt.getMonth() == m - 1 && all.some(e => e.y == dt.getFullYear() && e.m == m && e.d == dt.getDate()) })
                }
            months.push({ m: m, name: app.monthName(m), mcol: (m - 1) % 4, mrow: Math.floor((m - 1) / 4), cells: cells })
            }
        return { months: months }
        },
    emptyYear() { return { months: [] } },

## Navigation
A view switch is just a new `mode` (the focus rect springs); a page turn is
a new navYear/navMonth/navKey. The model derives from those, so navigation
only sets state — and `today()` is a return to the defaults.

segments.html:
goMode(m: string) { this.selectedId = -1; this.mode = m; if (m == "year") this.yearSeen = true },
    pickDay(key: string) {
        const d = app.parseKey(key)
        this.navKey = key; this.navYear = d.getFullYear(); this.navMonth = d.getMonth() + 1; this.selectedId = -1; this.mode = "day"
        },
    pickMonth(m: number) { this.navMonth = m; this.selectedId = -1; this.mode = "month" },
    today()       { this.navYear = 0; this.navMonth = 0; this.navKey = "" },
    step(dir: number) {
        const a = app.parseKey(this.anchorKey)      // paging keeps the anchor day coherent
        if (this.mode == "year") {
            const y = this.year + dir
            this.navYear = y
            this.navKey = y + "-" + (a.getMonth() + 1) + "-" + Math.min(a.getDate(), new Date(y, a.getMonth() + 1, 0).getDate())
        } else if (this.mode == "month") {
            let m = this.month + dir, y = this.year
            if (m < 1) { m = 12; y-- } else if (m > 12) { m = 1; y++ }
            this.navMonth = m; this.navYear = y
            this.navKey = y + "-" + m + "-" + Math.min(a.getDate(), new Date(y, m, 0).getDate())
        } else {
            const n = new Date(a.getFullYear(), a.getMonth(), a.getDate() + dir * (this.mode == "week" ? 7 : 1))
            this.navKey = app.keyOf(n); this.navYear = n.getFullYear(); this.navMonth = n.getMonth() + 1
            }
        },
    selectEvent(id: number, key: string?) {
        this.selectedId = id; this.openSection = 0
        if (key != null) this.navKey = key
        },
    closeDetail() { this.selectedId = -1 },

segments.md:
## Drag to reschedule
Pointer capture, plus the runtime's click rule, give click-vs-drag for
free: a gesture that moved is a drag and clicks nothing, so the block's
`onClick` fires only on a real tap. The threshold below is the app's own
(when the ghost appears), not a click suppressor. A drop writes through
the dataset's mutation API, so it wakes the derived model exactly like a
title edit — no copy to rebuild.

segments.html:
// the event being moved, a snapshot for the ghost, the grab offset

    dragId: number = -1,
    dragging: boolean = false,
    dropKey: string = "",
    dragTitle: string = "",
    dragCat: string = "",
    dragTimeLabel: string = "",
    dragW: number = 0,
    dragH: number = 0,
    grabDX: number = 0,
    grabDY: number = 0,
    downX: number = 0,
    downY: number = 0,

    startDrag(id: number, title: string, cat: string, timeLabel: string, w: number, h: number, gx: number, gy: number) {
        this.dragId = id; this.dragTitle = title; this.dragCat = cat; this.dragTimeLabel = timeLabel
        this.dragW = w; this.dragH = h; this.grabDX = gx; this.grabDY = gy
        this.dragging = false; this.dropKey = ""; this.downX = this.pointerX; this.downY = this.pointerY
        },
    dragMove() {
        if (this.dragId < 0) return
        if (!this.dragging) {
            const dx = this.pointerX - this.downX, dy = this.pointerY - this.downY
            if (dx * dx + dy * dy > 16) this.dragging = true
            }
        if (this.dragging) { const cell = this.cellAt(this.pointerX, this.pointerY); this.dropKey = cell != null ? cell.key : "" }
        },
    armDrag() {
        // The chip's hold fired: lift the ghost at once, before any movement —
        // on touch this is the moment the claim engages, and the pickup should
        // be visible while the finger is still parked.
        if (this.dragId < 0) return
        this.dragging = true
        const cell = this.cellAt(this.pointerX, this.pointerY); this.dropKey = cell != null ? cell.key : ""
        },
    dropDrag(px: number, py: number, canceled: boolean) {
        if (this.dragId < 0) return
        // A drag never clicks — the runtime's own rule (a gesture whose pointer
        // wandered past slop resolves to no click), so the drop just commits —
        // but never an interrupted one: on touch the browser may take the
        // gesture for a scroll (a quick swipe over a chip), and that release
        // must not move the event to wherever the finger happened to be.
        if (this.dragging && !canceled) this.commitDrop(px, py)
        this.dragId = -1; this.dragging = false; this.dropKey = ""
        },
    cellAt(px: number, py: number) -> object {                         // invert the span mapping: screen point → grid cell
        const col = Math.floor((px - this.pad - this.gutter) / this.colW + this.c0)
        const row = Math.floor((py - this.barH - this.headH) / this.rowH + this.r0)
        return this.cal.value.grid[app.clamp(row, 0, this.monthRows - 1) * 7 + app.clamp(col, 0, 6)]
        },
    commitDrop(px: number, py: number) {
        const events = app.data.value != null ? app.data.value.events : []
        const idx = events.findIndex(e => e.id == this.dragId)
        if (idx < 0) return
        const ev = events[idx], p = ["events", idx]
        const cell = this.cellAt(px, py)
        if (cell != null) { const d = app.parseKey(cell.key); app.data.set([...p, "y"], d.getFullYear()); app.data.set([...p, "m"], d.getMonth() + 1); app.data.set([...p, "d"], d.getDate()) }
        if (this.blockness > 0.5) {          // a time view: also reschedule from the drop height
            const dur = ev.end - ev.start
            let s = Math.round(((py - this.barH - this.headH - this.grabDY) / this.rowH * 1440) / 15) * 15
            s = app.clamp(s, 0, 1440 - dur); app.data.set([...p, "start"], s); app.data.set([...p, "end"], s + dur)
            }
        },

## Chrome
Declared last for the top z-order. Three zones: brand + theme switch hug the
left, Today + the view tabs hug the right, and the date nav floats near the
centre, clamped so it never rides into either side.

segments.html:
bar: View [ width = { app.width }, height = { app.barH }, fill = { provided("theme").background },
        stroke = { [null, null, stroke(1, provided("theme").line), null] },   // the rule under the bar is its own bottom edge

        // Tab follows the bar as it reads. On one row the date nav sits between
        // the two clusters, so it is visited between them; on two rows it is
        // the second row, which tree order already gives.

        tabOrder() { return app.barNarrow ? this.tabDefault() : [top.brand, top.themeSwitch, nav, top.today, top.tabs] },

        // Row 1 is the first 60px band — fixed, not barH-derived, so the narrow
        // tier's second row doesn't drag it downward. Brand and the appearance
        // switch hug the left, Today and the view tabs the right.

        top: View [ x = 20, width = { app.width - 20 - (app.barNarrow ? 12 : 20) }, height = 60,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 16, align = center ],

            // where each cluster ends, in the bar's coordinates — the date nav
            // floats between them

            leftEnd: number = { this.x + (app.showTheme ? this.themeSwitch.x + this.themeSwitch.width : this.brand.x + this.brand.width) },
            rightStart: number = { this.x + this.today.x },

            brand: View [ height = 22,
                layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 5 ],

                Text [ fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, letterSpacing = { -0.02 * fontSize }, wrap = false, textFill = { gradient("90deg", provided("theme").accent, provided("theme").accentSecondary) }, text = "Declare",
                    onClick() { app.navigate("apps/homepage/homepage.declare") }
                    ],
                Text [ fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, letterSpacing = { -0.02 * fontSize }, wrap = false, textColor = { provided("theme").text }, text = "Calendar",
                    visible = { !app.brandCompact } ]
                ],

            // Light / System / Dark — the house control, with the house marks:
            // drawn icons that share one disc and one stroke, rather than three
            // typed glyphs from unrelated corners of whatever font the platform has.

            themeSwitch: AppearanceSwitch [
                visible = { app.showTheme },
                dark = { app.isDark },
                input(v: boolean) { app.themeMode = v ? "dark" : "light" }

            // its pill along a normalised lane so a resize snaps instead of
            // skating, and brings tab stops, arrow roving, and the shared look.

            x = { app.barNarrow
                ? (app.width - this.width) / 2

            prev:  NavArrow [ dir = -1 ],
            title: Text [ width = { app.dateW }, textAlign = center, fontSize = 16, wrap = false,
                fontWeight = semibold, textColor = { provided("theme").text }, text = { app.periodLabel } ],
            next:  NavArrow [ dir = 1 ]
            ]
        ]
